findings.title: Bullet badges in topic title lose their top offset and inherit a new line-height
findings.body: The diff deletes the `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule and adds `line-height: 1.5` to `.extra-info-wrapper`. Bullet badges have no line-height of their own, so they now inherit 1.5 and lose the 5px top margin. Both changes shift where bullet category badges sit in the topic title. The PR does not mention either change, and nothing in this diff makes `.extra-info-wrapper` a flex container that would justify a vertical-alignment change. This is an unexplained visual regression.

findings.title: small-action becomes a flex row without sizing the description, and floats stop working
findings.body: `.small-action` is now `display:flex`, but `.small-action-desc` gets no `flex-grow`/`flex: 1`. It therefore sizes to its content rather than filling the row. The old `padding-left: 4em` that reserved room for the avatar is replaced by `0 1.5%`. Floats are ignored on flex items, so `.topic-avatar { float: left }` is a no-op and, if the `button` is a direct child (the `button` selector at this nesting level suggests it is), `button { float: right }` at line 309 no longer pushes it to the right edge. The message box will not fill the post width and the button placement will change. This needs a visual check; as written it looks like an unverified layout change.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms-align-items property
findings.body: `-ms-align-items` is not a property in any browser's CSS. The declaration is silently dropped, so it does nothing, and it misleads readers into thinking an IE-specific alignment declaration is being emitted. The IE10 equivalent is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already on line 120. The line should be removed.

findings.title: order(2) has no effect unless an ancestor of .extra-info-wrapper is a flex container
findings.body: `order` only affects children of a flex or box container. This PR does not turn any ancestor of `.extra-info-wrapper` into a flex container, so the new `@include order(2)` is dead CSS unless an ancestor is already flex in the base stylesheet or markup. The author should confirm that the rule does something or drop it.

findings.title: Title claims a performance optimization; description is placeholder and scope is undocumented
findings.body: The PR title says it optimizes header layout performance, but a float-to-flexbox layout change makes no performance measurement and the diff does not explain any performance gain. The description is only 'Test 5'. The diff also changes topic posts (`.small-action`), topic titles (`.extra-info-wrapper`, the removed bullet margin, the new line-height) and category badges, none of which are part of the header. Reviewers have no rationale for these visual changes and no before/after evidence. The description should state the scope, the intended visual changes and how they were verified.
